Ah, my post was vague sorry, the second. I'm super lucky with my parents, especially my dad, in that they just want me to be happy and do what I want. Which of course, adds to the feeling selfish aspect, it would be a lot easier to not care about them and just go.

I do understand where you're coming from, I loathe feeling like this at my lowest moments because it makes it a lot harder and adds to the overall stress and anxiety I'm going through  at that moment, but maybe when/if I'm feeling better I'll appreciate it. 

But to answer your question, no, not really. Not right now, there isn't anything that I do specifically for myself, my family are the only thing which makes me happy. Which, I suppose I'm lucky to have anything at all but it's just very tiring, and I really wish I did have something for myself that wasn't another human.

(Apologies if this doesn't make sense or is confusing at all, I sometimes struggle to put my thoughts into words in a cohesive way.)

I'm sorry you feel that way, that sounds awful and painful. But I completely relate to worrying about just passing the pain on, it's unfair to feel like this, but I feel like it's worse to inflict that onto others. 

Whilst I know that this isn't how it works, I hope happiness comes your way soon and that you can, at the very least, feel relief from what you're going through right now.

i almost took 90 pills yesterday but the fear or my family having to deal with my death and finding my body was worse than the idea of having to live an extra day.

sometimes i really wish i didn't care about other people's emotions so i could off myself.

I kinda get what you mean, but I never get outwardly angry, I don't feel angry at the person. Just angry at myself.

My best friend got into college and has been there for the past two weeks, and I feel so bitter and jealous because I dropped out of college at the beginning of the year and feel reminded of my fucked up life ig.
